subtopic: The Argand Plane and Polar Representation
title: Polar (trigonometric) form

board_content.text: Writing z as r(cos + i sin)
With $r=|z|$ and $\theta=\arg z$; and $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$ to go back.
Standard polar uses a $+$ between cosine and sine.
Method: (1) find $r$, (2) find $\alpha=\tan^{-1}|y/x|$, (3) place $\theta$ by quadrant, (4) write it out.
The conjugate keeps the same modulus and negates the argument.

segments_english.text: With modulus and argument in hand, we can write any nonzero complex number in polar form, the launchpad for rotation and powers.
Polar form is z equals r times, in brackets, cosine theta plus i sine theta. This is sometimes abbreviated r cis theta.
Here r is the modulus and theta is the argument. And to convert back to Cartesian, just use x equals r cosine theta and y equals r sine theta.
A formatting rule that examiners love to test: standard polar form uses a plus sign between the cosine and the sine terms.
So r times cosine theta minus i sine theta is not standard polar form. If you meet it, rewrite it using cosine of minus theta plus i sine of minus theta, which restores the plus.

The conversion method is four clean steps. One, compute r. Two, compute the reference angle alpha. Three, place theta in the correct quadrant. Four, write out r times cosine theta plus i sine theta. Step three is where most marks are lost.
The conjugate in polar form is elegant: it keeps the same modulus r but flips the sign of the angle, giving r at angle minus theta.
That matches the reflection picture from before: reflecting across the real axis leaves the distance unchanged and simply negates the direction.

segments_hinglish.text: Modulus aur argument haath mein hone se, hum kisi bhi nonzero complex number ko polar form mein likh sakte hain, jo rotation aur powers ka launchpad hai.
Polar form hai z equals r times, brackets mein, cosine theta plus i sine theta. Ise kabhi kabhi r cis theta likha jaata hai.
Yahan r modulus hai aur theta argument. Aur Cartesian mein wapas jaane ke liye bas x equals r cosine theta aur y equals r sine theta use karo.
Ek formatting rule jise examiners test karna pasand karte hain: standard polar form cosine aur sine terms ke beech plus sign use karta hai.
To r times cosine theta minus i sine theta standard polar form nahi hai. Agar mile, to ise cosine of minus theta plus i sine of minus theta se rewrite karo, jo plus wapas laata hai.

Conversion method chaar clean steps hai. Ek, r nikaalo. Do, reference angle alpha nikaalo. Teen, theta ko sahi quadrant mein rakho. Chaar, r times cosine theta plus i sine theta likho. Step teen mein sabse zyada marks jaate hain.
Polar form mein conjugate elegant hai: ye same modulus r rakhta hai par angle ka sign flip karta hai, deta hai r at angle minus theta.
Ye pehle wali reflection picture se match karta hai: real axis par reflect karne se distance same rehti hai aur bas direction negate ho jaati hai.
